recentItems.title: SATNAC 2026 | SA urged to develop homegrown AI solutions: Liabo Setho reports
recentItems.description:
As the global race for artificial intelligence accelerates, industry leaders are warning against simply importing solutions developed elsewhere. Delegates converged at the Southern Africa Telecommunications Networks Applications conference in the Drakensberg, KwaZulu-Natal.

They highlighted the need for localised innovation, arguing that South Africa's AI future must be shaped by local needs, local research and local talent.

SABC News Reporter Liabo Setho has more.

recentItems.title: Potato prices surge to R77 per 10kg bag
recentItems.description:
The price of potatoes has jumped by 15%, reaching R77 for a 10-kilogram bag at local fresh produce markets.

Industry body Potatoes SA says that the spike is being driven by a combination of rising operational costs, ongoing supply chain disruptions, and the unpredictable effects of climate change.

However, Potatoes SA says that this specific price hike is relatively normal for this time of the year

recentItems.title: COSATU Congress | COSATU expected to vote for its top six: Katlego Legodi reports
recentItems.description:
The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) is set to begin voting for its top six leadership positions this afternoon at its 15th National Congress in Kempton Park. This follows a chaotic start to the congress last month, which collapsed due to eligibility disputes. Out of 12 potential candidates initially selected only 10 remain on the ballot. 

For more on the congress, let's bring in SABC News economics reporter, Katlego Legodi

recentItems.title: Housing expected to dominate November 4 local government elections in Blikkiesdorp
recentItems.description:
Housing is expected to be a key issue in the November 4th local government election. In Blikkiesdorp, a temporary relocation area in Delft on the Cape Flats, some residents say they've spent nearly twenty years waiting for permanent housing.

Their story highlights the challenge facing municipalities, as demand for housing continues to outstrip supply.

recentItems.title: Impeachment Inquiry | Makashule shares thoughts on the matter
recentItems.description:
The Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) is asking the Western Cape High Court to overturn Parliament's decision to rescind the nomination of Advocate Thandazani Madonsela SC as chief evidence leader in the Phala Phala impeachment inquiry. The EFF argues that the Section 89 Committee acted unlawfully and irrationally, claiming it reversed its recommendation only after President Cyril Ramaphosa objected to Madonsela's involvement. 

Advocate Mfesane ka Seboto, for the EFF, says the central question is whether the committee had a lawful basis to rescind its decision when, according to the party, no material circumstances had changed. 

Parliament is defending the decision, insisting the committee acted within National Assembly rules and had the power to reconsider its recommendation.

recentItems.title: AKA, Tibz Murders | State calls a new witness to testify
recentItems.description:
The state has called a new witness to testify in the murder trial of rapper Kiernan "AKA" Forbes and businessman Tebello "Tibz" Motsoane at the High Court in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal. 

Seven men are accused of killing Forbes and Motsoane on Durban's Florida Road in February 2023.

The have pleaded not guilty to the murder, attempted murder and possession of unlawful firearms and ammunition charges.

recentItems.title: Former Mayor claims political motivations behind corruption case against him
recentItems.description:
Former Knysna Mayor Thando Matika says the corruption case against him is politically motivated. He was addressing SACP supporters outside the local Magistrate’s Court following his release on R20 000 bail. He was arrested alongside the Acting Municipal Manager and Acting Chief Financial Officer nearly two weeks ago. 

The trio are accused of soliciting kickbacks worth over half a million rand from a businessman who was awarded a security contract by the municipality. The case has been postponed to 2 December for further investigation.
